## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Apaṇṇakajātaka* (Ja 1) is the opening text of the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya, which traditionally commences a corpus of 550 birth stories [Appleton 2010; Norman 1983]. According to the frame narrative, the discourse concerning truth was delivered by the Buddha while residing at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative of the past, the Bodhisatta is depicted as a wise caravan leader [Appleton 2010]. The prose commentary includes an exegesis on the word *kantāra* ("wilderness") [Norman 1983], and the narrative includes the standard "story of the present" (*paccuppannavatthu*) [Appleton 2010].

An early version of the narrative later identified as this jātaka appears in the *Pāyāsi Sutta* of the *Dīgha Nikāya*, where the story is narrated after the Buddha's *parinibbāna* by the disciple Kassapa without an identification of the characters with the Bodhisatta [Appleton 2010]. In modern scholarship and translation, English renderings of the text have been prepared by Robert Chalmers and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus identifies Pali-internal text reuse between the canonical verse material of Ja 1 and the commentary, *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), sharing five matching passages, the longest aligning segments §2.1–3.1 of Ja 1 with §900–902_0 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus reports cross-language parallels or alignments in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
